## Certified close — merged as ae4f6c1a07a9666adfbd7882e06d11dade61966a (Gerrit change 2350, LLM-Review +1 / Verified +1)

Closed `--class plan_defect --ref ae4f6c1a07a9` (pinned immutable SHA, never `origin/main`).
`verify-signature --kind completion-verifier` -> **certified**, `verified-at-sha:ae4f6c1a07a9666adfbd7882e06d11dade61966a`.

Independent verification worktree detached at ae4f6c1a07a9; all evidence in-codebase (no `[non-codebase]` provenance required).

### Liveness anchors (proving the tool body actually executed)

Every failure envelope below was produced by driving the REAL registered MCP tool
(`build_server().call_tool(...)`), not a unit stub. Two anchors distinguish "reached the
failure path" from "failed earlier for an unrelated reason":

- **Positive anchor** — `render_workflow{"workflow":"review_skeleton"}` (a real built-in) returns
  **SUCCESS** (a rendered mermaid flowchart) through the identical call path and argument name.
- **Negative anchor** — `render_workflow{"wrkflow":...}` (wrong argument name) raises a pydantic
  `ValidationError` with **no** `McpEnvelopeError.envelope` at all. So an `{"error": ...}` envelope
  is only reachable by binding args successfully and executing the tool body.

### AC evidence — codes an actual caller receives

| Case | Call | `error` code |
|---|---|---|
| AC1 | `render_workflow{"workflow":"nonexistent-wf"}` | `not_found` |
| AC2 | `get_workflow_status{"run_id":"nonexistent-run"}` | `not_found` |
| AC2 (2nd site) | `get_workflow_status{"run_id":"no-such","ticket_id":<real>}` | `not_found` |
| AC2 (3rd site) | `get_workflow_result{"run_id":"nope"}` | `not_found` |
| invalid_input | `render_workflow{"workflow":"badwf"}` (found, unparseable) | `invalid_input` |
| liveness | `render_workflow{"workflow":"review_skeleton"}` | SUCCESS |

Message shape preserved: `"nonexistent-wf: workflow 'nonexistent-wf' not found (no such file, ...)"`.

- **AC1** [x] — `not_found`, distinct from `llm_unavailable`, through the real read tool.
- **AC2** [x] — `not_found` on all three run-lookup sites (`_locate`, `status()`, `result()`).
- **AC3** [x] — genuine outage still `llm_unavailable`, classifier fields POPULATED:
  `_structured_llm_failure(LLMUnavailableError('bedrock: provider 503 ServiceUnavailable'))` ->
  `{"error":"llm_unavailable","resolution_class":"NEEDS_INVESTIGATION","retryable":false,
  "diagnostic":{"exception_type":"LLMUnavailableError",...}}`. The bare `WorkflowError`
  EXECUTE base likewise stays `llm_unavailable` — the base was deliberately NOT flipped.
- **AC4** [x] — EXHAUSTIVE enumeration of all 24 `LLMError` subclasses: every
  `error_code_for` result is a `KNOWN_ERROR_CODES` member (non-members = `[]`). The
  `_structured_llm_failure` emitted range over that same subtree is exactly
  `{invalid_input, llm_unavailable, not_found}`, all members.
- **AC5** [x] — `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_workflow_error_codes_dbca.py`, 9 tests, all
  asserting the `error` CODE (each also asserts `!= "llm_unavailable"` and membership).
- **DD1** [x] — 1134 passed across `tests/unit/workflow/` + `tests/interfaces/contracts/`;
  `make lint` RC=0 (incl. complexity ratchet), `make typecheck` RC=0 (684 files).
- **DD2** [x] — `docs/mcp-reference.md` Failure shape names `not_found` / `invalid_input` and
  states the outage case stays `llm_unavailable`; `scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py` updated in
  lockstep and `tests/unit/test_gen_mcp_reference.py` (14) + surface-marker/api-surface gates
  (36) pass, so doc and generator are in sync.

### Mutation check — the classes are distinguished FROM EACH OTHER, not merely non-success

Each production edit reverted individually; seeds anchored to line starts and confirmed applied
via a non-empty `git diff --numstat`; pytest **return code** recorded (not eyeballed output); the
positive liveness anchor stayed SUCCESS under every mutant.

| # | Mutant | RC | Code the caller then receives |
|---|---|---|---|
| M0 | baseline no-op | 0 (9 passed) | not_found / not_found / not_found / invalid_input |
| M1 | `runs.py` name-miss -> pre-fix `WorkflowParseError` | **1** | AC1 flips to **`invalid_input`** |
| M2 | `runs.py` `_locate` -> pre-fix bare `WorkflowError` | **1** | AC2 flips to **`llm_unavailable`** |
| M3 | `runs.py` `status()` run-absent -> bare `WorkflowError` | **1** | AC2b flips to **`llm_unavailable`** |
| M4 | `_errors.py` remove the whole classifier branch | **1** (6 failed) | ALL FOUR -> `llm_unavailable` — the original bug reproduced exactly |
| M5 | collapse `not_found` -> `invalid_input` | **1** (4 failed) | all four -> `invalid_input` |
| M6 | collapse parse/validation/version -> `not_found` | **1** (2 failed) | all four -> `not_found` |
| M7 | drop the two codes from `KNOWN_ERROR_CODES` | **1** (5 failed) | codes unchanged, membership fails |

M5 and M6 are the anti-vacuity result: collapsing the two caller classes **into each other** —
which leaves every case still an error, and still not `llm_unavailable` — is killed in both
directions. So the oracle pins the specific code, not merely "an error was raised".

### Surviving mutants (reported honestly; neither vacates an AC)

- **M8** — reverting `_mcp_llm._structured_llm_failure` to the hard-coded `"llm_unavailable"`
  literal survives the dbca file AND `test_llm_disposition_plumbing.py` +
  `test_mcp_error_envelope_heldout.py` (32 passed, RC=0). This is a real oracle gap for Fix-Plan
  step 4, but it vacates no AC: AC4 holds under either form (`llm_unavailable` is a member), and
  AC1/AC2 flow through the generic `_envelope_error` guard, not this site. In practice the three
  call sites are `review_code` / `verify_completion` / `review_plan`, none of which resolve a
  workflow name or `run_id`, so the delegation is taxonomy consistency / future-proofing rather
  than a live behaviour change. Recorded as residual, not a blocker.
- **M9** — dropping the `source=` prefix from `WorkflowNotFoundError.__init__` survives. No AC
  covers message text (AC5 explicitly requires code-not-message assertions); the shipped code
  does preserve the shape, confirmed live above.

### Close class

`plan_defect` — "the design/plan itself was wrong" (`docs/ticket-model.md`). The blanket
`LLMError -> llm_unavailable` mapping shipped by 8a31-e1c3-cf31-4239 (biomedical-upper-tench,
commit 77f1c4011c83) never carved out the workflow caller-input subtree; nothing previously
worked and regressed, so not `regression`. Matches the sibling closes wolflike-chevroned-haddock
and dear-name-ladle. `caused_by` link to 8a31 already recorded.

Release blocker on c066-c496-7012-4a39 (0.13.0) is cleared: the client-visible codes an external
caller receives are demonstrated end-to-end through the shipped MCP tools.
